us: Bessent launches Outcast at Treasury · Five lifelines determined · ~60 designations · Dollar-expulsion threat
effects: ~60 designations across five jurisdictions · Rial record low at 2.02M/$ · Oil −$2 on the day · No countries named
iran: Madanizadeh: Tehran 'fully prepared' · Ghalibaf dismisses 'bluster' · PGSA blacklists 45 ships
tldr: The promised economic D-Day arrived as scaffolding: five sectoral determinations covering digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping, and roughly sixty designations across five jurisdictions — with no countries named for secondary penalties, no Chinese banks touched and little market reaction. Bessent promised a major financial-institution designation by week's end and demanded every Bank Melli branch close; Tehran answered that it was 'fully prepared' as the rial opened at a record 2.02 million to the dollar. Pakistan's army chief spent the day meeting Iran's leadership while its port authority blacklisted 45 ships for defying Hormuz transit rules.

events.title: Bessent at Treasury: 'sever every economic lifeline… until Tehran stands alone'
events.summary: Treasury formally began 'Operation Economic Outcast': five sectoral sanctions determinations under E.O. 13902 against Iran's digital-assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors, plus ~60 OFAC designations across the UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland — including the Hong Kong-based Sweet Ocean procurement network and shadow-fleet oil brokers. General licenses for remittances and cultural/academic exchange were suspended, and OFAC issued an advisory on the risks of bowing to Iran's Hormuz transit demands. Bessent called the rollout 'a warning shot' with a defined 'cure period'; no country was named for secondary penalties and markets showed little reaction.

events.title: Tehran unmoved: Madanizadeh 'fully prepared,' Ghalibaf says 'no one believes their bluster'
events.summary: Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh told IRINN the government is 'fully prepared for this economic war' — 'you will fail this time too' (Fars) — and warned 'if they take any action, they should expect an attack from us' (ISNA); on state television he said Iran's defense 'is no longer so defensive; the enemies should wait for an attack.' Parliament speaker and lead negotiator Ghalibaf posted that partners 'don't take these statements into account' and told media 'no one believes their bluster.' Pezeshkian, hosting Munir, said Washington must 'correct its tone and approach… relying on force and bullying will only complicate the process.'

events.title: Bank Melli closure demanded; financial-institution sanction promised 'by the end of this week'
events.summary: In his remarks Bessent demanded 'every Bank Melli branch must be shuttered,' vowed a 'zero-leakage approach' expelling any money-laundering facilitator from the dollar system, and said every country gets 'a defined timeline' before Treasury acts unilaterally. He teased 'a major announcement of a financial institution being sanctioned by the end of this week.' The list conspicuously omitted Chinese banks — analysts read the restraint as calibration ahead of Xi Jinping's expected visit next month; Beijing called the pressure tactics unhelpful.

events.title: PGSA lists 45 ships in Hormuz transit crackdown
events.summary: Iran issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the strait without permission, listing 45 vessels it said violated its rules and threatening fines, detention or confiscation, with retaliation promised for any ship-to-ship transfers involving listed ships (Reuters). The second such list since the Persian Gulf Strait Authority's first 'noncompliant vessels' roster published Sunday.

events.title: Munir works the Tehran circuit: Ghalibaf, Rezaei, Momeni — no breakthrough
events.summary: Pakistan's army chief met parliament speaker Ghalibaf, who blamed Washington for failing to honor the 'Islamabad memorandum'; SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei told him the US 'must change its behavior and take concrete steps toward fulfilling the conditions of the memorandum of understanding' (IRIB); he also met interior minister Momeni, accompanied by Pakistan's interior minister Naqvi, and was expected to stay overnight to meet Pezeshkian. CNN confirmed Trump phoned Munir last week to ask Islamabad to push both sides back to talks.

events.title: Rial opens at record 2.02M/$ hours before the rollout; oil slips ~$2
events.summary: Iran's currency hit a record low as trading opened ahead of the announcement — 2.02 million rials to the dollar against an official central-bank rate around 1.5 million. Oil fell more than $2 a barrel on the day despite the rollout, and broader markets showed little reaction. AP tallied war-economy costs at home: rice up ~60% and beef +150% since February, IMF forecasting GDP contraction above 5%.

events.title: Houthis claim Red Sea missile strike on Saudi tanker; Bahri confirms vessel involved
events.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile hit on a tanker off Yanbu, and Saudi national shipping company Bahri said one of its tankers was involved in an incident in the Red Sea (CNN). No damage assessment or independent confirmation in the window; the claim foreshadowed the Ash Shishah tanker strike reported early the next UTC day.

events.title: Oman FM due in Tehran as Hormuz joint-management plan reportedly nears
events.summary: Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Al-Busaidi is scheduled to visit Iran Tuesday to discuss the strait and regional developments; AP reports Iran and Oman are in the final stages of a plan for joint management of the waterway — the diplomatic track running beneath the sanctions launch.

events.title: Trump: Iran 'COMPLETELY COLLAPSING'; Netanyahu congratulates the campaign
events.summary: Trump posted Monday that Iran is 'COMPLETELY COLLAPSING' while pressing leaders by phone with 'specific requests' to cease trade with Tehran. Israeli PM Netanyahu publicly congratulated Trump and Bessent: 'You justly exact a steep price from that cruel dictatorship and from those who assist its continued aggression.'

dossier: Night count: 25th consecutive without confirmed strikes inside Iran. CENTCOM blockade accounting carried unchanged at 70 redirected / 3 disabled / 2 boarded; Crypto Briefing (Aug 24, citing centcom.mil) alone reports 71 diverted plus 40+ humanitarian vessels passed through — centcom.mil not directly verifiable this run, confirm tally against next CENTCOM release. From Bessent's Q&A: asked why no immediate penalties — 'Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?'; 'we are level-setting with every country… We know who they are. They know who they are.' Treasury remarks: 'zero-leakage approach,' 'the clock is ticking,' teams from Treasury, State and 'War' engaging counterparts worldwide. Designation detail: Sweet Ocean Industrial (HK) network of 20+ entities/persons procuring for sanctioned Malek Ashtar University (laser optics, accelerators); Shenzhen Huamei and BRE Line (HK branch) hit for missile/nuclear support; front companies Feili, Minvur, Feisu feeding shadow-banking exchanges (Amin, Sadaf). UAE cutoff context: announced last week after the missile attack on the emirate; Bessent called it 'not a coincidence' and predicted a 'broad array' of countries follows. Timing caveats: Madanizadeh's state-TV line ('enemies should wait for an attack') and IRGC spokesman Mohebbi's chokepoint threat moved on the Reuters wire published Aug 24 but were re-filed in the Aug 25 report — treat timing as approximate across the boundary; Hegseth's Monday remarks ('no choice' but talks; kinetic strikes not ruled out) likewise straddle and are owned by the Aug 25 report. China: Foreign Ministry called sanctions unhelpful, pledged to protect its interests; ICG's Wyne — Trump has 'largely given China a pass.' Analyst lines: MEI's Eyre — enforcement 'absent any follow-up… highly unlikely'; Leiden's Gawthrope — Russia/China won't cut ties; CIP's Toossi — blockade hurts but Iran hasn't capitulated. Largest partners left unpenalized per AP: China, Turkey, UAE. Also same day: US lifted its state sponsor of terrorism designation on Syria (context move). Hegseth last month put US war cost at $37.5B. Reuters' original 45-ships story was captcha-blocked this run; filed via the Al-Monitor wire copy at medium confidence.
